title: C1757 — Engine Mount Control Solenoid Connector
introduction:
An engine-mount control solenoid sounds mysterious until its wiring gets an address book. I use this reference to match the connector’s cavity marks with the listed supply-side and powertrain-control circuit descriptions. Those labels explain the connections’ stated jobs without telling us how the mount itself operates.

Start with the component identity table, use the drawing’s marks to choose the matching Cavity row, and read across that row before moving to the pigtail listing. The housing identifiers connect those sections.

This is an identification and wiring-reading guide, with no engine-specific applicability stated. It supplies no physical access, connector-release, probing, operating-value or replacement procedure. The physical viewing direction, gauge convention and meanings of Box, Size and Used are unspecified. Keep the printed alternatives and codes intact rather than turning them into a wiring or repair decision.

edits.why: The drawing places vertically stacked cavity marks within a rounded surround, with a larger rectangular structure on the left and a projection on the right. I use that outline to keep the marks aligned with the table. The illustration identifies features on the page; it does not establish a physical viewing direction or show how to release the connector.

Match each cavity mark to its row, then keep the circuit identifier, color, gauge, Function and terminal entry together. The function descriptions distinguish the fuse-or-circuit-breaker supply reference from the powertrain module’s active-mount connection. Preserve the stated alternative: this sheet does not choose the applicable protection arrangement, define the control waveform or establish a fault from a symptom.

I connect the pigtail listing to the drawing by comparing Engineering Shell with the Fpn and Hard Shell entries above. Service Part identifies the listed service item; Image names its illustration file. The pin-assignment and pigtail gauges are separate reference entries, so the pigtail row does not by itself settle wire choice or explain how to splice or replace the connector.
